summary: Transient GPU scarcity following short-lived high-concurrency bursts causing increased p99 latency and allocation failures in dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:

Customer ParcelVision reported intermittent increases in p99 latency for short inference requests served from their dedicated pool. The incidents correlate with short (~10-60s) spikes of high concurrency from many small streams. During spikes we observe allocation failures for new batched slots and transient 503/504s. Impact: user-visible request latency and a small number of failed requests.

Impact:
- ParcelVision experiencing p99 latency increase from ~180ms to 1.6s for short text-complete routes.
- ~0.7% request errors (5xx) during spike windows lasting 30-90 seconds.
- Customer reports degraded user experience in UI flows during spike windows.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool id: dp-09c7 (ParcelVision reserved pool)
- Region: prod-us-west primary, fallback to prod-us-east
- Serving runtime version: 2.14.1
- Autoscaler: v1.6.0 (policy: conservative, min_slots=4, max_slots=40)

Observed behavior:
- Rapid increase of short, concurrent streams (<200 token each) from a single tenant over 10-60s.
- Autoscaler scaled up but lagged ~45-75s before new GPUs accepted slots.
- During scale-up some worker processes reported "slot allocation timeout" and returned 503.
- KV cache churn increased, leading to transient memory pressure on several GPUs.

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler should add capacity within SLO and the serving-runtime should handle short spikes by queuing/batching without causing allocation failures or sustained p99 degradation.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) From a client in prod-us-west, start 150 concurrent short-stream requests (avg 40 tokens) over 20s using rw-instruct-13b pinned to dedicated pool dp-09c7.
2) Observe autoscaler activity, GPU slot allocation logs, and request latencies.
3) Repeat with burst sizes of 75, 150, 300 to observe scaling thresholds.

Logs and pointers:
- Grafana dashboard: dashboards/prod/dp-09c7/throughput-and-latency
- Traces: tracing-service/trace/parcelvision/2026-03-09T16:22Z (sample)
- Worker logs (scrubbed): s3://redwood-logs/dp-09c7/2026-03-09/worker-alloc.log
- Autoscaler events: metrics-store.autoscaler.dp-09c7.events (noted scale-up delay at 16:21:34 UTC)
steps_to_reproduce: Start 150 concurrent short requests (40 tokens avg) over 20s against dedicated pool dp-09c7
Watch autoscaler events and worker logs for slot allocation timeouts
Scale burst sizes to determine threshold where allocation failures begin
observed_metrics_snippet: p99 latency spike from 180ms to 1.6s; error rate 0.7% in 16:20-16:24 UTC; autoscaler scale-up started at 16:21:34 UTC and finished at 16:22:50 UTC; 12 allocation timeout events logged across 3 workers.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Aisha: Customer reported first instance; provided initial logs and Grafana links.

2026-03-10 11:08 - SRE (Marcelo): Replayed synthetic burst in staging with same autoscaler policy; observed scale-up latency ~40s; reproduced allocation timeouts when burst exceeded 140 concurrent short streams.
2026-03-10 13:40 - Runtime eng: Heap/KV cache thrashing observed on GPUs during spikes; cache eviction rate rose 8x causing increased host-GPU sync activity.
2026-03-11 02:22 - Scheduler: Noted slot fragmentation in dp-09c7; many small-stream allocations left unusable tiny free gaps (fragmentation) causing new large allocations to wait.

2026-03-11 08:05 - Autoscaler: Scale decisions were correct but the pool infra experienced transient provisioning queue due to concurrent reclamation jobs from another tenant (noisy background checkpoint writer logged in dp-09c7 at 16:20 UTC).

2026-03-12 14:10 - Hypothesis consolidated: Combined effects of short-stream fanout (many small allocations), KV cache churn, and concurrent background maintenance from another tenant produced transient GPU resource scarcity and allocation timeouts. Autoscaler reacted correctly but could not bridge the immediate delta fast enough.
hypotheses: Short-lived high-concurrency spikes create many small slot allocations that increase scheduling overhead and fragmentation, slowing placement and causing allocation timeouts.
KV cache churn increases GPU memory pressure and triggers additional host<->GPU synchronization, which amplifies allocation latency.
Background maintenance (checkpoint writer) from a different tenant in same pool temporarily reduced effective GPU capacity (noisy neighbor).
actions_taken: Notified on-call pool infra team and temporarily increased burst capacity for dp-09c7 (+2 slots) at 2026-03-10 12:05 UTC
Applied temporary scheduler policy tweak to prefer packing small streams into fewer slots for dp-09c7 at 2026-03-11 04:30 UTC
Worked with customer to add client-side exponential backoff for rapid retrying short requests
Disabled a non-critical checkpoint writer job identified in logs for 15 minutes to observe baseline impact; noted immediate reduction in allocation timeouts
workaround: Recommended customer implement short-window client-side rate limiting/backoff for bursts above 120 concurrent short streams. We applied temporary scheduler packing and increased burst capacity for their pool which reduced errors to 0.12% in subsequent tests.
next_steps: Eng: implement faster transient burst handling in autoscaler (proposal tracked in github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/issues/119) to shorten scale-up reaction time for sub-90s spikes
Runtime: reduce KV cache thrash by introducing eviction hysteresis for small-stream workloads; prototype patch in runtime PR 4892
Scheduler: implement fragmentation compaction during low-load windows to prevent tiny free-gap accumulation
SRE: create a runbook entry for noisy-background-maintenance detection and temporary throttling to protect dedicated pools
resolution: In progress - temporary mitigations reduced customer-visible errors; long-term fixes assigned to Eng squads. Follow-up scheduled: eng design review 2026-03-16. Customer notified and provided mitigation guidance.
resolution_notes: Temporary scheduler packing + short-term capacity bump reduced error rate from 0.7% to 0.12% for ParcelVision during controlled replays. Engineering action items opened for autoscaler and runtime changes. Recommend treating as P1 until autoscaler patch is validated in staging.
